Ontology_AssayAndWorkflow_prompt.notes: The experiment is a metaproteomics analysis of ancient paleofeces. While no specific enrichment ontology term from the provided list was used, the search parameters are specifically tuned for aged protein degradation (oxidation and deamidation). The 'mod_metaproteomics' hint is added due to the nature of the sample (ancient feces/environmental community).

organism: human paleofeces dating from the Bronze Age to the Baroque period
noncellular_sources: We subjected human paleofeces dating from the Bronze Age to the Baroque period (18th century AD) to in-depth microscopic, metagenomic, and proteomic analyses.
scope: Paleofeces samples (ID 2610, 2604, 2611, 2612) and a blank control sample to highlight any contamination were resuspended in 800 μL 5% (w/v) sodium dodecyl sulfate (SDS), 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB, pH 8.5) and disrupted at 4°C using three 2.8 mm ceramic beads (QIAGEN, USA) and a Precellys 24 homogenizer (Bertin Corp, USA) at 6500 rpm for 30 s.

Ontology_SampleSourceAndScope_prompt.notes: The proteomics analysis was performed on total protein extracts derived from paleofeces (coprolites). While the samples contain a mixture of human, microbial, and dietary proteins, the processing (SDS resuspension and bead disruption) describes a total extract/lysate approach rather than a specific subproteome or affinity purification.

evidence: We subjected human paleofeces dating from the Bronze Age to the Baroque period (18th century AD) to in-depth microscopic, metagenomic, and proteomic analyses.
Paleofeces samples (ID 2610, 2604, 2611, 2612) and a blank control sample to highlight any contamination
The four paleofeces samples can be macroscopically differentiated into three samples containing a high amount of fibrous plant material (2610, 2604, 2611) and one more homogeneous sample (2612)

Radiocarbon analyses date the roughly structured samples to the Late Bronze Age (2610) and Iron Age (2604, 2611)... the fine-textured paleofeces 2612 sampled in an Iron Age mine dates to the Baroque period (18th century AD)
